claims.text: Pre-oxidation forms a coherent oxide layer on FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings.
The pre-formed oxide layer is thermally stable under high-temperature sliding wear conditions.
The oxide layer reduces direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings have lower wear and friction than as-deposited coatings at high temperature.
As-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coatings initially lack a pre-formed oxide layer.
A controlled pre-oxidation treatment can produce a uniform, adherent oxide scale.
The proposed mechanism applies to sliding wear at approximately 500–700°C.
The protective oxide layer is enriched primarily in oxidation-prone elements such as Cr.
The stable oxide scale acts as a barrier that passivates the coating surface.
Surface passivation by the oxide scale suppresses the initiation of plastic deformation.
Surface passivation by the oxide scale suppresses abrasion.
Suppression of direct contact, plastic deformation, and abrasion lowers friction and wear rates.
Pre-oxidized coatings will show lower mass loss or shallower wear tracks than as-deposited coatings at high temperature.
Pre-oxidized coatings will show lower coefficients of friction than as-deposited coatings at high temperature.
Differences between pre-oxidized and as-deposited coatings will be negligible at lower temperatures.
The oxide-layer effect is expected to be minimal at room temperature or under conditions that do not favor rapid oxidation.
Improved wear performance should correlate with oxide-layer continuity, adherence, thickness, and composition.
